title: Environment Setup for the Linear and Logistic Regression Tutorial
description: Import NumPy, Matplotlib, and scikit-learn models, preprocessing utilities, metrics, and datasets, then set NumPy's random seed and Matplotlib plot defaults.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Import `math`, `numpy`, `matplotlib.pyplot`, and scikit-learn utilities for train/test splitting, feature scaling and polynomial expansion, linear and logistic regression models (`LinearRegression`, `Ridge`, `Lasso`, `SGDRegressor`, `LogisticRegression`), and `Pipeline`.

Import regression and classification evaluation metrics (`mean_squared_error`, `r2_score`, `confusion_matrix`, `roc_curve`, `auc`, `classification_report`) and the `load_breast_cancer` and `load_iris` dataset loaders.
Seed NumPy's random generator with the supplied value, set `plt.rcParams` for `(6, 4)` figures and grid lines, and print `"Environment ready."`.

Look at lines 9-11 and 17: `StandardScaler`, `PolynomialFeatures`, and the five `linear_model` estimators plug into `Pipeline` objects. Setting NumPy's random seed makes every synthetic data draw repeatable.

steps.question: What output does this setup cell print when run?
steps.answer: It prints `Environment ready.` on line 23 after importing the libraries and configuring NumPy and Matplotlib.
